en: Mount Pulag, not Mount Apo, is the highest mountain in the Luzon island group.
Taal Volcano, often mistakenly called the smallest, is actually the lowest volcano in the world by elevation.
Taal Volcano, not Mayon Volcano, holds the record for the most historical eruptions in the Philippines.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, not the much shorter Pasig River.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, surpassing Lake Lanao in total surface area.
The Philippine Trench, not the Manila Trench, contains the deepest point in the Philippine Seas.
Mount Kanlaon, not Mount Mayon, is the most active volcano in the Visayas island group.
Palawan is geographically located outside the Pacific Ring of Fire, unlike most other Philippine provinces.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park is located in the Sulu Sea, not the Philippine Sea.
Mount Apo, located in Mindanao, is the highest mountain in the entire Philippine archipelago, not Mount Pulag.
Unlike the rest of the country, Baguio City has a subtropical highland climate rather than a tropical one.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River empties directly into the South China Sea, not the Pacific Ocean.
